ops.title: SECURITY: spawned-session lane authenticates nothing — the parent verifies itself
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.1 security re-review; present in shipped v0.20.x.

`internal/wire/spawned.go:155-161` calls `trust.PeerCredentials(config.Conn)` on the **parent's own**
end of the socketpair and `trust.Verify(peer, nil)` against a floor-only requirement. Peer
credentials on a self-created socketpair name the *creator* — so this is the parent verifying itself.
The gate authenticates nothing, and reads as protection where there is none. The repo already proves
the mechanism: `handoff_test.go`'s "peer is not the parent" case fails `proveHandoff` on a
self-created pair for exactly this reason.

Impact: combined with the program path being same-UID writable (`~/.daemonkit/bin/<name>` under the
phase-4 STABLE verdict) and `validateExec` checking only absolute-and-clean, a same-UID attacker who
replaces the executable at that path owns the spawned business lane's payloads.

The nonce does not close it: `DAEMONKIT_SPAWNED_NONCE` travels in the child's environment, which any
same-UID process reads via KERN_PROCARGS2 — daemonkit's own comment at
`internal/proc/executable.go:93` says so.

Cmd.Exec must verify the child IN PLACE, never a staged copy: App Group entitlements derive from the
launched bundle path.

ops.text: The self-verification at internal/wire/spawned.go:155-161 is deleted
The spawned lane's documented property is directional confinement (the pair was fd-passed to a process this parent exec'd), not peer identity
The nonce is documented as an fd-mixup defense, not authentication, with the KERN_PROCARGS2 reason stated
Either Cmd.Exec verifies the suspended child in place before release, or the residue is documented and owner-acknowledged
